thread:
incident-bot: Pager triggered: genqueue error rate spiking in eu-prod (~5xxs across fastgen). Severity: P1. Pager -> jamal. Bridge: https://call.example/xyz :rotating_light:
jamal: I'm on the bridge, pulling logs now. joining in 30s.
lauren: Thanks Jamal — ops on standby to scale replicas if needed. what's the customer impact?
jamal: High-level: some requests are returning 502/503; affecting ~12% of requests to eu-gen endpoints. No data loss. Trend started ~03:12 UTC.
alice: We should draft an initial status page + customer DM. I'll take initial copy and queue for legal.
statuspage-bot: Suggested initial status page template available: https://status.example/drafts/1766543210
alice: Draft below — quick review pls. will publish once legal signs off.
```
Initial update (investigating) — 03:18 UTC
Summary: We are investigating elevated error rates affecting text generation requests in the EU region. Some customers may experience failed requests (502/503). Engineers are on the bridge and mitigation is in progress.
Customer impact: Intermittent request failures for ~12% of EU gen traffic. No data loss or security impact identified.
What we're doing: On-call engineers are diagnosing the root cause and scaling capacity as a mitigation. We'll provide updates every 15 minutes or as we have significant changes.
Next update: ~03:33 UTC
```
jamal: Minor wording: change "scaling capacity" -> "scaling serving capacity (replica bump)". Otherwise OK.
kevin-legal: Quick legal scan — nothing sensitive. Suggest removing "customers may experience" -> "some requests may fail" (slightly clearer). ok from legal.
alice: Updated draft with edits, ready to publish on my mark.
maria: Ops note: we rolled a replica bump at 03:22 UTC, genqueue threads show fewer backpressure signs but error rate still above baseline. Keeping bridge open.
lauren: Good — once published, set monitor alert thresholds to mute noisy pages for correlated retries. Also schedule canary routing to alternate region if rate doesn't decline in 20 mins.
alice: Publishing initial update now. Published: https://status.example/incidents/1766543210 (Initial update published, 03:25 UTC) :white_check_mark:
statuspage-bot: Initial update posted and subscribers notified.
jamal: Continuing root cause analysis — logs indicate a downstream cache invalidation spike causing KV lookups to time out intermittently.
lauren: Ops: we've enabled a short TTL fallback for the cache and are watching. If error rate drops below 2% we can start ramping down temporary capacity.
alice: Posting 15m update (03:40 UTC):
```
15-minute update — 03:40 UTC
Status: Mitigation in progress
Summary: We deployed a short TTL fallback for the caching layer and temporarily increased serving replicas. Error rate has fallen from ~12% to ~4%. Some customers may still see intermittent failures.
Actions: Engineers continue to monitor and validate that errors do not spike when we scale replicas down.
Next update: ~04:00 UTC or sooner if resolved.
```
kevin-legal: wording fine.
maria: Monitoring: error rate trending down, request latency stable. No further regression detected in logs, continuing validation.
lauren: Throttling rule temporarily relaxed for retry bursts to reduce client-side pressure.
alice: If we see sustained <2% for two consecutive checks, we'll prepare resolved copy.
jamal: Root cause postmortem draft started on the bridge. Looks like a cache cascade from a malformed TTL update during a deploy.
statuspage-bot: Reminder: include RCA link when posting resolved.
alice: Final resolved copy ready, pls ack and I'll publish.
```
Resolved — 04:02 UTC
Summary: The incident affecting EU text generation requests has been resolved. A configuration change to the caching layer during a deployment caused elevated error rates; engineers deployed a TTL fallback and temporarily increased serving capacity which returned error rates to normal.
Customer impact: Intermittent 502/503 errors for up to ~12% of EU generation requests from ~03:12–04:00 UTC. No data loss or security impact.
What we changed: Reverted the TTL change and applied a short-term fallback. A follow-up postmortem (RCA) will be published within 72 hours with root cause and remediation steps.
Status: Resolved
```
lauren: Ack, looks good.
kevin-legal: Approved.
maria: Verified metrics look normal for 10+ mins post-fix.
ajamal: Thanks team. I'll finish the RCA notes and link them in the status incident.
alice: Published resolved notice and linked RCA draft: https://status.example/incidents/1766543210/resolved — closing thread. :sparkles:
